channel.title: Hypewire
channel.description: What people are talking about in AI, entertainment, gaming and tech, refreshed daily.

item.title: GTA VI is out and has a 99 on Metacritic, the joint highest score the site lists
item.description: Grand Theft Auto VI rolled out worldwide from November 18 in New Zealand to the Americas on November 19, with a 99 on Metacritic.

item.title: Anthropic closes its first trading day up 17% after a record IPO
item.description: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50 and closed at $97.17 on their Nasdaq debut, 17% above the $83 IPO price, Forbes reports.

item.title: Hunger Games prequel opens today with a $100 million-plus debut in sight
item.description: Sunrise on the Reaping opens November 20 on about 3,900 US screens, with BoxOfficePro's panel forecasting $100 million to $120 million.

item.title: Google launches Gemini 4 Neon with a 1 million token context window
item.description: Google released Gemini 4 Neon, its new model, at $3 per million input tokens and $15 per million output, rolling out in its API and Gemini apps.

item.title: GTA VI launch draws nearly 8 million live viewers and breaks a Twitch record
item.description: StreamCharts reports nearly 8 million concurrent viewers across five platforms for the GTA VI launch, and it broke Valorant's Twitch record.

item.title: Nvidia stops shipping H200 chips to China after a $115.8 billion quarter
item.description: Interim CEO Colette Kress said Nvidia plans no further licensed H200 shipments to China, after revenue more than doubled to $115.8 billion.

item.title: First trailer for Artificial casts Andrew Garfield as Sam Altman
item.description: Neon released the first trailer for Luca Guadagnino's Artificial, a drama about the power struggles at OpenAI.

item.title: Apple's new MacBook Pro is its first laptop with a touchscreen
item.description: Apple's new MacBook Pro has a touch-enabled ProLED XDR OLED display and is listed from $2,899, NBC News reports.

item.title: Meta's Muse AI reportedly read Signal messages through Android notifications
item.description: Reuters and Ars Technica report that Meta's Muse assistant could read encrypted Signal messages on Android through push notifications.

item.title: GTA VI runs at 30 frames per second on consoles, even on the PS5 Pro
item.description: GTA VI is capped at 30 frames per second on consoles, and Rockstar says even the PS5 Pro is not powerful enough for its simulation at 60.

item.title: Jensen Huang says he would return to Nvidia, but its chair says the board won't
item.description: Huang said he is open to returning as CEO if the board wants it; Nvidia's chair said the board will not reinstate him.

item.title: GPT-6.2 Astra ranks second behind Claude as early reviews of OpenAI's models split
item.description: Artificial Analysis ranks GPT-6.2 Astra No. 2 behind Claude Fable 5.2, while some power users have panned the release, VentureBeat reports.

item.title: Citi, PNC and Citizens say customers carry the losses from third-party AI agents
item.description: Three US banks changed their terms so customers are responsible for losses caused by outside AI agents with account access, even if hacked.

item.title: Robert Pattinson is the new James Bond in Denis Villeneuve's 007 film
item.description: Amazon MGM Studios named Robert Pattinson as James Bond for the first Bond film made under Amazon, directed by Denis Villeneuve.

item.title: Disney raises its 2027 content budget 9% to $26 billion and licenses films to Netflix
item.description: Disney plans to spend $26 billion on content in 2027 and roughly triple its Disney+ international originals over three years, C21 Media reports.

item.title: PHP fixes seven critical flaws, including one that can allow remote takeover
item.description: The PHP project released emergency security updates for all supported versions, fixing flaws that can allow remote code execution on some setups.

item.title: New York, LA and Chicago schools weigh dropping Google Search over AI features
item.description: Three of the largest US school districts are looking at alternatives after Google said schools that opt out of its AI features will lose Search.

item.title: GTA VI could reach PC in early 2027, a report says
item.description: GamesBeat, citing five sources, reports that GTA VI will launch on PC in the first few months of 2027. Rockstar has not announced a date.

item.title: UK loses its fight to keep its Apple encryption order secret
item.description: A UK tribunal ruled the government failed to show that confirming its technical capability notice to Apple would harm national security.

item.title: Ubisoft lays off 166 employees at its Montreal and Quebec City studios
item.description: Ubisoft has cut 166 jobs across its Montreal and Quebec City offices, Instant Gaming News reports.

item.title: Google's Gemini can now use apps on your Mac to finish tasks
item.description: Gemini for Mac can now operate apps, files and websites in the background to complete multi-step tasks, asking approval before key actions.

item.title: Palo Alto Networks buys AI startup Applied Compute for $4.5 billion in stock
item.description: Palo Alto Networks agreed to buy Applied Compute, a year-old startup that runs custom open-weight models on company data, in an all-stock deal.

item.title: Marvel drops 11 Avengers: Doomsday posters, a month before release
item.description: Marvel released 11 character posters for Avengers: Doomsday, plus a featurette on Robert Downey Jr.'s return as Doctor Doom.

item.title: Taylor Swift returns to the CMA stage for the first time in 13 years
item.description: Swift performed a mashup of 'I Knew It, I Knew You' and her debut-era 'Our Song' at the 60th CMA Awards in Nashville.

item.title: Netflix names Peter Rice as its new content chief
item.description: Netflix has named veteran TV and film executive Peter Rice as content chief, with a reported hands-on role in its film division.

item.title: GTA VI's eight Game Awards nominations now come with a 99 review score
item.description: GTA VI leads The Game Awards with eight nominations, including Game of the Year, and its reviews have now landed.

item.title: Broadcom patches a critical VMware vCenter flaw rated 9.8 out of 10
item.description: Broadcom fixed an authentication bypass in VMware vCenter's directory service, tracked as CVE-2026-123890, with no workaround available.

item.title: OpenAI says its models are helping redesign parts of its AI chips
item.description: OpenAI says an AI-generated circuit redesign cut a chip part's estimated area by about 15% in its chip work with AMD.

item.title: California bans Waymo robotaxis from freeways, and Waymo pauses them nationwide
item.description: California's DMV barred Waymo's driverless cars from state freeways, calling them an imminent hazard; Waymo paused freeway rides in all markets.

item.title: Microsoft unveils seven of its own AI models at Ignite, aimed at OpenAI and Anthropic
item.description: Microsoft launched seven in-house AI models at Ignite 2026, including MAI Code 2 and Code 2 Flash for software work.

item.title: Stallone biopic I Play Rocky goes wide with a $15 million to $20 million forecast
item.description: Amazon MGM's I Play Rocky expands nationwide this weekend after earning nearly $1 million on fewer than 30 screens.

item.title: Apple's iCloud, App Store and Apple Pay go down after an internal update
item.description: An Apple outage broke iCloud sign-in for users and disrupted the App Store, Apple Music, Apple Pay and AppleCare on November 17.

item.title: Google opens its Genie 4 world model to AI Ultra subscribers
item.description: Google's Genie 4 lets AI Ultra subscribers generate interactive worlds, change them with text while exploring, and hear responsive audio.

item.title: YouTube will add estimated group viewers on TVs to its view counts
item.description: YouTube will count estimated viewers watching together on connected TVs, using statistical modelling rather than cameras or microphones.

item.title: Netflix Games confirms another round of layoffs
item.description: Netflix's gaming division has carried out a new round of layoffs, Instant Gaming News reports; no headcount was given.

item.title: Ebenezer is forecast to drop about half in its second weekend
item.description: Johnny Depp's Ebenezer is forecast at $8 million to $13 million in its second weekend, falling to third as the Hunger Games prequel arrives.

item.title: N-able confirms hackers accessed a server in its email security cloud
item.description: N-able said unknown attackers accessed one server in its Mail Assure and SpamExperts hosted cloud, and it disabled management tools.

item.title: Canal+ seeks 137 million euros from Disney over former subscribers' emails
item.description: Canal+ is suing Disney in Paris, alleging it used emails of customers who activated Disney+ through Canal+ to sign them up directly.

item.title: Crimson Desert wins eight Korea Game Awards, including Game of the Year
item.description: Pearl Abyss's Crimson Desert took eight prizes at the Korea Game Awards, including the top award.

item.title: Apple's Black Friday event offers gift cards up to $300 from November 27
item.description: Apple's four-day Black Friday event runs November 27 to 30, with US gift cards of up to $300 on eligible purchases, MacRumors reports.

item.title: Google will keep Gemini chats for two months even with history turned off
item.description: Gemini users can now opt out of training without losing history, but temporary chats will be kept for about two months instead of 72 hours.

item.title: 007 First Light wins Game of the Year at the TIGA Awards
item.description: IO Interactive's James Bond game 007 First Light was voted Game of the Year by attendees at the UK's TIGA Awards.

item.title: MindsEye developer Build A Rocket Boy reportedly owes 62 million pounds
item.description: A new filing shows Build A Rocket Boy, the studio behind MindsEye, owes about 62 million pounds, Instant Gaming News reports.
